title: House Robber
description: Max sum of non-adjacent elements. At each house: rob (prev2 + n) or skip (prev1). Classic 1D DP with O(1) rolling scalars.

notes: Recurrence: dp[i] = max(dp[i-1], dp[i-2] + nums[i]) — either skip i or take i and lose i-1.
Both bases are 0 (no houses robbed yet); prev1 ends up holding the answer.
Update order matters — assign prev2 = prev1 BEFORE prev1 = curr, or you overwrite the value you still need.

questions.q: The recurrence for House Robber is:
Why cannot we rob two adjacent houses?
options: Problem constraint — adjacent houses trigger the alarm

questions.q: Space complexity of the rolling-variable version?
What do prev2 and prev1 start as?

exercises.prompt: Fill in the rolling-variable House Robber.

blanks.hint: rob this house: add to dp[i-2]

L3.prompt: Write `rob(nums)` returning the max sum you can collect without taking two adjacent elements. Use O(1) space. Log `rob([2, 7, 9, 3, 1])`.
hints: At each house: max(skip = prev1, rob = prev2 + n).
Roll forward — assign prev2 = prev1 BEFORE overwriting prev1.
